title: Rav Gada
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rav Sheshet’s attendant. In [Eruvin 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.11b.13), the Exilarch’s servants imprisoned him. Rav Sheshet, who was blind, stood at the gate and called, “Gada, come out.” They released him, and he came out. In [Shabbat 145b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.145b.8), after a remark by Rav Yosef, Hyman quotes a separate statement from Rav Gada according to Dikdukei Soferim. His Gemara reads Rav Gaza. “Once I went there and made Babylonian kutach, and all the sick people of the West asked me for it.”[^1]

notes.text: [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.145b.8.5) glosses בריחי as “the sick.” The consulted Shabbat text reads Rav Gaza. Heilprin gives the attendant under [Gada](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=832&lang=en) and the kutach passage under [Gaza](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=852&lang=en). The [Dikdukei Soferim page](https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/hF923F9uFWAC?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA345) shows Gaza in the printed text and Gada in its manuscript column.
